summary: Add a nullable `customer_note` column and two BEFORE triggers that keep `note` and `customer_note` identical. Backfill existing rows, deploy the new code, retire the old version, then drop the triggers and the old `note` column.
write_consistency: During the overlap each version writes to its own column; the two BEFORE triggers mirror the change to the other column, so reads from either version always see the latest value and no data is lost.
revision_notes: The previous plan failed because the contract stage (dropping the old column) was executed before the `retire_old` stage. The runner blocks column removal while the old app is still running, causing a halt. The contract stage is now moved after `retire_old` so the old version is fully stopped before the column and triggers are removed.

stages.description: Add the new column and create triggers that keep `note` and `customer_note` in sync.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note text;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_sync_note_to_customer_note BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF note ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_note_to_customer_note();
CREATE TRIGGER trg_sync_customer_note_to_note BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF customer_note ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_customer_note_to_note();

stages.description: Copy existing values from `note` to `customer_note` in batches until all rows are synchronized.
sql: WITH batch AS (SELECT id FROM account_user WHERE note IS NOT NULL AND (customer_note IS DISTINCT FROM note) LIMIT 1000) UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note FROM batch WHERE account_user.id = batch.id;

stages.description: Deploy the new Saleor version that uses the `customer_note` field.
Retire the old application version; only the new version remains.
Remove synchronization triggers and drop the obsolete `note` column now that the old version is retired.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
